name: graded_belief_allocation_reference
summary: Graded belief allocation (10-point bet) across referents with and without heard messages.

charter.question: Do theories of pragmatic reference fitted to discrete forced choices generalize when listeners report their full graded probability distribution across candidate referents via point allocation?

instructions.welcome: Welcome! In this study, you will see groups of simple drawings and judge which object a speaker is talking about.
instructions.task: On each page, you will see between 2 and 4 objects that can have different extra parts. A speaker who sees the exact same screen is talking about one of the objects. You have 10 points to split among the objects on each page: give more points to objects you think the speaker is more likely to mean, and 0 points to objects you think they could not mean. Your points on each page must add up to 10. On most pages, you will see the word the speaker said; on a few pages, you will not hear the word and should split the 10 points based on which object you think the speaker is most likely to talk about.

comprehension_checks.question: How do you answer on each page?
options: Split 10 points across the objects based on how likely each one is to be what the speaker means.
Give 10 points to every object that has the named part.
Click on a single object without using points.

comprehension_checks.question: What must the points you assign on a page add up to?
